title: Checkpoint: regimes, sizing and honest testing

questions.prompt: Stock at 30.00, ATR 14 = 0.75, stop = 2 × ATR. You risk 150 USD. How many shares?

options.explanation: No: that uses a 1 × ATR stop of 0.75. The stop is 1.50.
No: that would need a 3.00 stop, which is 4 × ATR.

questions.prompt: Rule: trending if net move over 20 candles ≥ 3 × ATR; low volatility if ATR ≤ 0.75 × its 100-candle average. Net move 40 pips, ATR 20 pips, average ATR 30 pips. Label?

options.explanation: No: 40 ÷ 20 = 2 ATR, below the 3 ATR needed for a trend.
No: 20 ÷ 30 ≈ 0.67, which is 0.75 or less, so low volatility.
Right: 2 ATR is below 3, and 20 ÷ 30 ≈ 0.67 is at most 0.75.

questions.prompt: 10 trades: one of +6R and nine of −1R. What is the average result per trade?

options.explanation: No: that leaves out the nine losses.
No: −1R is the median, the middle trade. The average is −3R ÷ 10.

questions.prompt: A plan needs RSI above 50, MACD above zero and price above SMA 20. What is a fair description?

options.text: Three separate confirmations that add up
options.explanation: No: all three come from recent closes, so they often agree for the same reason.

options.text: Closely linked readings of recent direction
options.explanation: Right: correlated indicators largely repeat one message.

options.text: A filter set that removes false signals
options.explanation: No: no combination of indicators removes false signals.

questions.prompt: In a walk-forward test, why judge only the joined test blocks?

options.text: They contain more trades than tuning blocks
options.explanation: No: they often contain fewer. The point is what the rules had seen.

options.text: They remove the need for a demo forward test
options.explanation: No: a forward test on a demo account is still the next step.

options.text: The rules never saw those candles in tuning
options.explanation: Right: the rules had not seen those candles when they were set.

questions.prompt: Which set of results is least likely to be fragile?

options.explanation: Right: neighbouring settings agree, so the result does not hinge on one number.
No: a lone peak with losing neighbours is a sign of overfitting.
No: without neighbours you cannot see how sensitive it is.
